record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Barth and Clunie [64] have constructed a bounded analytic function in D with a level set component of infinite length; this component is highly branched. Can one construct a bounded analytic function with an unbranched level set compo- nent of infinite length? (K. F. Barth and J. G. Clunie)

evidence.quote: Barth and Clunie [64] have constructed a bounded analytic function in D with a level set component of infinite length; this component is highly branched.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. For a non-constant analytic function $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ and a value $w\in\mathbb{C}$, the level set of $f$ at $w$ is $L_w(f)=\{z\in\mathbb{D}: f(z)=w\}$; a level set component is a connected component of $L_w(f)$. Such a component is called unbranched if it is homeomorphic to an arc (equivalently, it contains no point at which $f-w$ vanishes to order greater than $1$, so that locally and globally the component is a simple curve with no branching). Its length is its $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

Question: Does there exist a bounded analytic function $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ possessing a level set component which is unbranched and has infinite length?
artifact.category_tag: Bounded analytic functions in the unit disc
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the 1982 Barth–Clunie construction of a bounded analytic function on the unit disc with a (highly branched) level set component of infinite length, but no source was found establishing or refuting the existence of such an example with an unbranched level set component. The current status is therefore unclear.

status_evidence.title: A bounded analytic function in the unit disk with a level set of infinite length (Barth–Clunie)
status_evidence.snippet: Barth and Clunie construct a bounded analytic function in D with a level set of infinite length; the construction yields a highly branched component.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the original (branched) construction but does not address the unbranched variant.
